caption:
Doubt can be the start of knowing.

Save this and test one belief this week.

From "Learn To Think For Yourself." Copy and paste the link in bio.

#thinkforyourself #descartes #criticalthinking #philosophy #mindset

text: “If you would be a real seeker after truth, it is necessary that at least once in your life you doubt, as far as possible, all things.”
Descartes did not doubt to be difficult.
He doubted to find what was solid.
Most of what we believe was handed to us.
Family, school, feeds, friends.
Handed down is not the same as tested.
Testing is how a belief becomes yours.
Doubt here is a tool, not a mood.
It asks: *How do I know this is true?*
Pick one belief you hold tightly.
Look for the best case against it.
If it survives, it is stronger.
If not, you learned something.
Which belief would you most hate to test?
This is the thread behind the book *Learn To Think For Yourself*.
Your own thinking is the whole point.
Practice the pause.
*Judge for yourself.*

caption:
Clarity starts with where you look.

Save this, then give one thing five minutes of undivided attention.

From "The 14-Day Clarity Reset." Copy and paste the link in bio.

#thinkforyourself #attention #clarity #mindfulness #selfawareness

text: “Attention is the rarest and purest form of generosity.”
She wrote this in a letter, not a lecture.
It was about how to truly be with another person.
Attention is the first thing we spend.
Most days we spend it before we choose to.
Clarity is not more information.
It is attention, held still long enough to see.
Try it with one thing today.
One conversation. One task. One thought.
No second screen.
When the mind wanders, that is not failure.
*Noticing* is the practice. Come back, gently.
You cannot think clearly about what you never look at.
Attention is where your own thinking starts.
What deserves your full attention today that has only had scraps?
This is the thread behind the book *The 14-Day Clarity Reset*.
Fourteen days of small, steady practice.
Give it your attention.
*See what becomes clear.*

caption:
It is not always the thing. Often it is the sentence about the thing.

Try it: rewrite one harsh thought more exactly.

From "The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech." Copy and paste the link in bio.

#innerspeech #selftalk #stoicism #mindset #thinkforyourself

text: “Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of them.”
The event happens once.
The retelling can happen a thousand times.
Listen to the words you use inside your head.
*Ruined. Always. Never. Idiot.*
Those are views, not facts.
Your inner voice is a narrator.
Narrators choose what to emphasize.
Epictetus did not say feelings are fake.
He said the judgment comes between the thing and the feeling.
Slow that gap down.
Ask: *What happened? And what am I adding?*
Change the sentence, and the weight changes.
Not by lying to yourself, but by being more exact.
What is one sentence you keep telling yourself that is a view, not a fact?
This is the thread behind the book *The Science of Learning Your Inner Speech*.
Learn to hear the narrator, and edit it.
Hear the voice.
*Then answer it.*

caption:
Not knowing yet is not failing. It is thinking.

Save this and write down the question you are living with.

From "Learn To Think For Yourself." Copy and paste the link in bio.

#thinkforyourself #rilke #criticalthinking #philosophy #selfreflection

text: “Be patient toward all that is unsolved in your heart and try to love the questions themselves.”
He wrote this to a young poet who wanted answers now.
The advice was to wait, and to keep asking.
We are trained to want answers fast.
A quick answer feels safe, even when it is borrowed.
A question you live with changes you.
An answer you borrow rarely does.
Thinking for yourself includes tolerating *not knowing yet.*
That is uncomfortable. It is also honest.
Keep one open question on your desk this week.
Let it sit. Let it knock.
Some answers arrive only after you have lived the question long enough.
Let yours arrive in your own voice.
Which unanswered question are you ready to stop rushing?
This is the thread behind the book *Learn To Think For Yourself*.
Your thinking, at your own pace.
Stay with the question.
*Own the answer.*
